Summary: We can remove the overlay from private Channel, Community, space and Project
Creator: usama virk
Description:
### *Overview*

A security/UI vulnerability exists where the full content of restricted/private areas (specifically Channels, Communities, Spaces, and Projects) can be viewed by a user who is not a member, by temporarily removing the obstructing overlay using the browser's "Inspect Element" developer tool.

### *Steps to Reproduce*

### Log in as a user *who is NOT a member* of a private Channel (or Project/Space).
### Navigate to the URL of the private Channel (e.g., {{[Insert Example URL Here]}}).
### The page will display a large overlay with a message like "This channel is private" or "Join to view content."
### Right-click on the screen and select *"Inspect"* (or use F12 / Cmd+Option+I).
### In the Elements/Inspector panel of the Developer Tools, locate the HTML element responsible for the overlay. 
### Right-click on the identified overlay element (e.g., {{<div class="private-content-blocker">}}) and select *"Delete element"* or *"Hide element"* (using {{display: none;}} CSS).

Summary: Enhancements & Fixes in Project Task and Comment Module (Reporter, Description Limit, Tagging, Comment Improvements, and Navigation Flow)
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Multiple functional and UI improvements are required in the *Project Task* and *Comment* sections to enhance user experience, traceability, and collaboration efficiency.
Below are the detailed issues and proposed enhancements:

h3. *1️⃣ Reporter Field in Project Task Module*

*Issue:*
Currently, there is no way to identify who created a specific task.

*Enhancement:*

* Add a *“Reporter”* field to automatically capture the name of the user creating the task.
* The field should be *system-generated* and *non-editable*.
* Display the *Reporter* column in the *Task Listing Page*.
* Add a *Reporter filter* in the filter panel to allow task filtering by creator.

*Expected Outcome:*
Each task should display the creator’s name, and users can filter tasks by Reporter.

h3. *2️⃣ Comment Section – Image Attachment Support*

*Issue:*
Currently, users cannot upload or attach images in the *comment section*, limiting effective bug reporting and communication.

*Enhancement:*

* Allow users to *attach images* (JPG, PNG, etc.) in comments.
* Uploaded images should be previewable within the comment thread.

*Expected Outcome:*
Users can share screenshots and visual evidence directly in comments.

h3. *3️⃣ Increase Description Text Limit*

*Issue:*
The task description field currently has a *limited character count*, which restricts detailed bug or feature reporting.

*Enhancement:*

* Increase the description character limit to *2000 characters*.

*Expected Outcome:*
Users can enter detailed descriptions without truncation issues.

h3. *4️⃣ Mentioning Team Members Using “@” Tag*

*Feature Request:*

* Implement an *@mention* feature within the *comment section*.
* Typing “@” should display a list of all project members.
* The tagged user should *receive a notification* when mentioned.

*Expected Outcome:*
Facilitates better collaboration and ensures the right people are notified promptly.

h3. *5️⃣ Comment Edit Option*

*Feature Request:*

* Add an *Edit* option in the comment section for users to update their own comments after posting.

*Expected Outcome:*
Users can correct or enhance comments without deleting and reposting them.

h3. *6️⃣ Comment Formatting – Space Retention Issue*

*Bug:*
When users add spaces or line breaks between paragraphs in comments, the spaces are *removed after saving*, affecting readability.

*Expected Fix:*
Ensure that all formatting (spaces, line breaks, etc.) is retained after comment submission.

h3. *7️⃣ Task Creation – Redirect Behavior*

*Issue:*
After successfully creating a new task, users stay on the same form with a success popup.

*Enhancement:*

* After successful task creation, automatically *redirect users to the Task Listing page*, highlighting the newly created task.

*Expected Outcome:*
Improves user flow and confirms task creation visually.

Summary: Send System Notification When Recipient Is Not in Sender’s Chat

* Verify notification delivery through the existing real-time system.

*Actual Result:*

* The project addition notification shows only an *"N" placeholder icon* instead of the profile picture of the person who added the user.

Summary: Shortcut hierarchy display issue in left sidebar causes confusion
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
When creating a shortcut (e.g., for a Space), the left sidebar displays only the *parent (Channel)* first and then the actual shortcut (Space). Due to limited sidebar width or long names, the *Space name is hidden*, and only the Channel name is visible.
This makes it appear as though the shortcut was created for the Channel instead of the Space.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Login to the application.
### Navigate to any *Channel* and open a *Space*.
### Create a *shortcut* for that Space.
### Check the *left sidebar* where the shortcut is listed.

*Expected Result:*

* The shortcut should clearly display the *full hierarchy* (e.g., _Community > Channel > Space > Project_) so users know exactly what entity the shortcut belongs to.
* If parent names need to be shown, they should follow a proper hierarchy format.
* Tooltip text should display the *complete hierarchy* for clarity when names are long or truncated.

*Actual Result:*

* The sidebar shows *Channel name first* and then the Space name.
* If names are long, only the Channel name is visible, making it look like a *Channel shortcut* instead of a Space shortcut.

*Impact:*

* Users may be confused, thinking they created a shortcut for the Channel instead of the intended Space.
* Affects navigation and user experience, especially in organizations with long naming conventions.

*Suggested Fix:*

* Display shortcuts with *proper hierarchy* for clarity (Community > Channel > Space > Project).
* Add a *tooltip* showing the full path when hovering over the shortcut.
* Consider truncating text smartly (e.g., ellipsis in the middle) instead of hiding key child names.

Summary: Notifications: Inconsistent profile icon size & alignment issues
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Multiple UI issues are observed under the *Notifications* section.

### *Profile Icon Size Inconsistency*

* When the same user sends a connection request, their profile icon appears *large*.

### *General Alignment Issues*

* Profile icons and notification text are not properly aligned vertically.
* Misalignment is clearly visible when comparing “connection request” vs “connection accepted” notifications.

### *Missing Date/Time Information*

* Notifications do not display *date or time* of occurrence.
* This makes it unclear *when* the notification was received.
* Example: If multiple requests/acceptances occur, the user cannot differentiate the sequence.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Go to *Notifications*.
### Trigger two events from the same user:
###* Send a connection request.
###* Accept the connection request.
### Compare both notifications.
### Observe that no *date/time* stamp is available.

*Actual Result:*

* Profile icon size differs between notifications.
* Notification components appear misaligned.
* No date/time shown with notifications.

*Expected Result:*

* Profile icons should have a *consistent size* across all notifications.
* Icons and text should be properly aligned.
* Each notification should display *date/time* for clarity on when it occurred.

Summary: Folder & File Management Issues – Case Sensitivity, Duplicate File Names, and Missing Delete Option
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
During confirmation testing of the File Sharing module, the following issues were observed related to folder and file management:

*Issue 1 – Case Sensitivity in Folder Names:*

* Users can still create folders with the same name but different letter casing (e.g., _“Example”_ and _“example”_).
* This leads to confusion and redundancy, as both folders are treated separately.
* *Expected Result:* Folder names should be case-insensitive, preventing duplicates with only casing differences.

*Issue 2 – Duplicate File Names Allowed:*

* Within the same folder, duplicate file names can be uploaded.
* This may overwrite files unintentionally or confuse users about which file is the latest.
* *Expected Result:* System should restrict duplicate file names within the same folder.

*Issue 3 – Missing Delete Option for Folders:*

* Currently, neither the folder creator nor the Super Admin can delete a folder once created.
* This limits content management and cleanup in File Sharing.
* *Expected Result:* Folder creators and Super Admins should have the ability to delete folders.

h3. *Steps to Reproduce:*

### Navigate to {{Spark → Channels → [Any Space] → File Sharing}}.
### Create folders with similar names but different casing (e.g., Example, example).
### Upload files with the same name in a single folder.
### Try to delete a folder as creator or Super Admin.

h3. *Actual Result:*

* Folders with the same name but different casing are allowed.
* Duplicate file names are accepted in the same folder.
* No option to delete folders exists.

h3. *Expected Result:*

* Folder names should be case-insensitive.
* Duplicate file names should not be allowed.
* Folder creators and Super Admins should be able to delete folders.

Summary: Restrict Invites in Unpublished Channels and Spaces
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Currently, in *Unpublished Channels and Spaces*, the *Invite button* is visible and functional. This leads to the following issues:

* Users can be invited to an unpublished Space/Channel.
* Invited users can *accept the invite*.
* However, after accepting, the Space/Channel is *not visible* to the user because it is unpublished.

This creates confusion and inconsistency in user experience.

*Expected Result / Feature Request:*

* The *Invite button* should not be displayed or should be disabled for *Unpublished Spaces/Channels*.
* Invitations should only be possible once the Space/Channel is *published and visible*.
* This ensures logical flow: if users are invited, they must be able to see and access the Space/Channel after accepting.

*Impact:*

* Prevents invalid invitations and confusion for users.
* Ensures consistent access control and better user experience.

Summary: Missing “No Data Found” Message in Connections Interface
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
In the *Connections* module, when there are no records under specific sections (Incoming Requests, Outgoing Requests, All Requests, or Connected), the interface currently displays a blank screen. This creates confusion for users, as they are unable to distinguish between an empty state and a potential loading or system issue.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Log in to the application.
### Navigate to *Connections*.
### Go to *Incoming Requests*, *Outgoing Requests*, *All Requests*, or *Connected* tabs where no records are available.
### Observe that the interface is blank with no contextual message.

*Actual Result:*
Blank screen is displayed when no data exists in a section.

*Expected Result:*
When no records are available, the interface should display a meaningful message such as:

* _“No incoming requests at the moment.”_
* _“No outgoing requests found.”_
* _“No connections available.”_
* _“No requests.”_

This will improve the user experience by clearly indicating the state of the data.

Summary: Request-to-Join Feature for Private Communities, Channels, and Spaces
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Currently, when a user (viewer role) tries to access a private community, channel, or space, they only see a private access screen with no option to proceed further. To improve usability and controlled engagement, a *"Request to Join"* feature should be introduced.

*Feature Requirements:*

### When a user views a private community, channel, or space, instead of just the private screen, a *"Request to Join" button* should be visible.
### Clicking the button will send a join request to the respective admin/creator of that community, channel, or space.
### The admin/creator should be able to view pending requests in their management panel.
### Admin/creator should have the ability to *approve or reject* join requests.
### On approval, the requesting user should be automatically added to the community/channel/space.
### On rejection, the user should be notified that their request was declined.

*Expected Result:*

* Users can send join requests for private communities, channels, or spaces.
* Admin/creator receives and manages join requests (approve/reject).
* Approved users gain access, rejected users get notified.

Summary: Issues with Invite Link Access Control and Member Status Handling
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
The invite link feature for Communities, Channels, and Spaces currently lacks proper validation and security controls.

* *Invite Link Reuse by Unauthorized Users*
** When an admin generates and sends an invite link to a specific user, the link can be shared further by that recipient.
** This allows *anyone* with the link to join the Community/Channel/Space without admin approval, which *violates security and privacy policies*.
** *Expected:* Admin should have to *approve join requests* before access is granted.
* *Invite Sent to Already Joined Members*
** If an admin sends an invite to a user who has already joined the Community/Channel/Space, the receiver still sees the option to "Join."
** This causes *confusion*, as users who are already members should instead see a message like *"You have already joined this Community/Channel/Space."*
** *Expected:* The system should detect existing membership and *disable the join option* for already-joined users and show *Joined* text..

*Expected Result:*

### Invite links should be restricted to *admin approval* before granting access. Links must be validated against the intended recipient, preventing unauthorized access if forwarded.
### Already joined users should receive a clear message stating *"You are already a member"* instead of being shown the *Join* button.

Summary: Add Ticket History Logging Feature (Similar to Jira)
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Currently, the system does not maintain a visible history log for tickets. Users are unable to view past actions (such as status changes, field updates, or comments). To improve transparency and traceability, a *ticket history feature* should be implemented similar to Jira.

This feature should log and display all key actions performed on a ticket, ensuring users can review historical updates at any time.

h3. *Expected Behavior:*

* Every action on a ticket should be logged (e.g., creation, status change, field updates, comments, assignment changes).
* History should be easily accessible from the ticket view.
* Display should include *timestamp, user, and action details*.
* History log should be read-only to maintain integrity.

h3. *Benefits:*

* Provides full traceability of ticket lifecycle.
* Improves collaboration and accountability across the team.
* Helps in debugging workflow issues by reviewing past changes.

Summary: No Option to Cancel Connection Request on Profile Page
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
After sending a connection request to a user, there is no option to cancel the request on the user’s profile page. Instead, the profile continues to show only the "Connection" state without allowing the user to withdraw/cancel the pending request. This causes inconvenience and makes the connection management process less user friendly.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Go to the application URL.
### Use the *search bar* to search for any user.
### Select the user from search results to open their *profile page*.
### Click *Connect* to send a connection request.
### Observe that after sending the request, there is *no Cancel Request button* on the same profile page.

*Expected Result:*
After sending a connection request, the user should see a *Cancel Request* option on the profile page to withdraw the request if needed.

Summary: Active Features Hidden Until Joining a Space – Misleading “No Feature Available” Message
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Currently, the *Active Features* of a Space do not show up unless the user has joined the Space. When a user has not joined, the Active Features section only shows the *count* and displays the text _“No feature available”_, which is misleading and not user-friendly.

This creates confusion because there are indeed active features, but they are hidden until the user joins.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Go to any Space without joining it.
### Check the *Active Features* section.
### Observe that only the count is shown, with the placeholder text _“No feature available”_.

*Actual Result:*

* Before joining, the Active Features section shows only a number and the message _“No feature available”_.
* After joining, the Active Features are displayed correctly.

*Expected Result:*

* If the user has not joined the Space, the UI should clearly indicate that features are restricted.
* Instead of _“No feature available”_, the interface should display a user-friendly message like:
_“Join this Space to view Active Features.”_

Summary: Missing Dynamic Character Limit Indicator in Title Fields for Community/Channel/Space/Project Creation
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Currently, when creating a Community, Channel, Space, or Project, the Title field does not display a live/dynamic character count. If a user enters a title longer than the allowed limit, the system only shows a "too long" error after clicking on form submission, instead of guiding the user while typing. This results in poor user experience.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Navigate to the creation form for a Community/Channel/Space/Project.
### In the Title field, enter a text string exceeding the allowed character limit.
### Attempt to submit the form.

*Actual Result:*
The form only shows a "too long" error message after submission.

*Expected Result:*

Summary: Space & Main Posts – Poll Text Misalignment, Poll Not Displaying with Images, Poll Option Position Shifting, and Category/Window Issues
Creator: Hamza Nasir
Description:
Multiple issues have been identified while creating posts (both in main feed and Space):

### *Poll Text Mixing with Main Text*
###* When entering text in the "Main Text" field, it also appears in the "Poll Text" field.
###* If text is added in the main text field first, it incorrectly reflects in the poll text field.
### *Poll Behavior After Posting*
###* If a poll is created with main text + poll text + poll options, only the main text is shown after posting; the poll is missing.
###* Poll only displays when text is entered directly into the poll text field along with poll options.
###* If poll text + image are added together, only the image displays; the poll is not visible.
### *Poll Option Position Bug in Published Post*
###* When a poll option is in the first position and selected, after refreshing the page, it shifts to the last position. This impacts user clarity and poll reliability.
###* Once an option is selected, *all options become disabled*. The user cannot unselect or change their choice.
### *Category Visibility & Filtering (Space Posts Only)*
###* Posts created with categories in Space do not display the category after publishing.
###* No option to filter posts by category, making categorization ineffective.
### *Create Post Window Behavior* 
###* After publishing a post, the "Create Post" window does not close automatically.
###* Instead, it remains open and shifts tab focus unnecessarily.
### *Post Editing Limitation:*
###* After publishing a post, users cannot edit it. Only the _Delete_ option is available.
### *Empty Post & File Upload Allowed (Space Post)*
###* Users can upload and publish empty posts by attaching only an image or file without any text.
###* Users can also upload and publish empty files (inside spaces and outside spaces).

*Steps to Reproduce:*

### Go to *Main Feed → Create Post* OR *Space → Posts → Create Post*.
### Enter text in the main field, then in the poll field with options.
### Optionally, add an image along with poll text.
### Select a category (if inside Space).
### Publish the post.
### Observe poll visibility, poll option position after refresh, category display, and create post window behavior.

*Expected Result:*

* Main text and poll text should remain independent.
* Poll should always display correctly with or without main text/images.
* Poll option order should remain consistent after posting/refresh.
* Categories should be visible on published posts and filterable.
* Create Post window should close automatically after successful publishing.
* Users should be able to edit published posts in addition to deleting them.
* Empty posts, empty files, and unsupported uploads should not be allowed.
